pages.text: The seawater had retreated far away. A wide muddy shore lay bare.
They wanted to dig clams for the evening soup. Mom said, "Water bubbles where clams are hiding."
Lolo ran off with a shovel. Riri crouched to look for holes first. "Dig a lot and they will appear." "We should dig only the right holes."
Lolo dug wildly here and there. Ten holes appeared.
Only water filled each hole. Lolo's basket was empty.
Riri marked each little hole with a shell. There were more than twenty markers.
Now it was hard to tell which holes were real clam holes. Riri's basket was empty too.
Water bubbled up in one of Lolo's holes. Riri saw it and opened her eyes wide.
Together, they dug down there. Out came one handful of clams, then two.
Clam soup steamed on the dinner table. One more shell turned up in Lolo's bowl. Mom pressed her apron tight, trying not to laugh.
